attrs.evidence: spec_release.mjs v0.3.0 releaseCore() + releaseId(); auditIdentity() perturbs every leaf of the core one at a time -- the denominator DERIVED by walking the core, not typed -- and requires each to move the identity, and perturbs the 3 declared non-core fields and requires each NOT to. Both halves: a one-way sweep passes over an identity that fails to bind, and a positive-only sweep passes over one that has grown to cover prose. Reproduced against v0.2.0's formula: 3 of 16 core leaves stuck, all three under `protocols`. Runs at ISSUANCE as well as verification, so a future edit to releaseCore that drops a member is refused at the moment it would be signed. Gate `gov-spec` and `gov-nest`; grid boolean release-id-binds-protocols, falsified by renaming all three protocols and requiring srel to move.
attrs.statement: A RELEASE IDENTITY A SECOND RUNTIME CANNOT RECOMPUTE IS NOT AN IDENTITY, IT IS A LOCAL HABIT. v0.2.0 built the spec_release_id preimage with `JSON.stringify(core, Object.keys(core).sort())`, and a JSON.stringify replacer ARRAY is an allowlist applied RECURSIVELY: the allowlist held the fourteen top-level core keys and none of `wire`, `verified_claim`, `nested_composition`, so the nested protocol map serialised as `"protocols":{}`. MEASURED: renaming all three protocol identifiers to EVIL-A/EVIL-B/EVIL-C left the preimage BYTE-IDENTICAL and the identity at srel-3ac8f6fc..., so the statement `the release identity binds the protocol identifiers` was false at the formula, though not a passing forgery because the names are separately CHECKED against the normative schema. This is also the class P4.1 through P4.3 spent three passes eliminating -- a canonicalisation only a JavaScript host reproduces -- reappearing in the file that names the specification. The preimage is `canonicalWire(release_core)` now: the same RFC 8785 encoder the wire protocol uses, whose conformance is established against six pinned upstream vectors as octets rather than against this file.
